abstract: Cultured neuron models are essential for studying neuronal biology and disease, yet it remains unclear how neuronal culture media shape the global proteome and protein turnover. Here, we compared human iPSC-derived neurons cultured in four different media: BrainPhys, DMEM/F-12, Neurobasal, or a 1:1 DMEM/F-12:Neurobasal mixture using label-free and dynamic SILAC proteomics. To enable protein turnover measurements in BrainPhys, we developed an in-house SILAC-compatible BrainPhys formulation that supported comparable viability and proteome coverage to commercial BrainPhys. BrainPhys produced a proteome and turnover landscape distinct from the other three media, which closely resembled one another. BrainPhys-cultured neurons showed lower relative abundance of DNA replication- and progenitor-associated proteins and higher relative abundance of synaptic and neuronal projection proteins, consistent with a more mature neuronal proteome. BrainPhys also globally prolonged protein half-lives, yielding a turnover profile more similar to later-stage primary neurons and in vivo brain. Despite their distinct basal proteomes, neurons cultured in different media exhibited a conserved proteomic response to acute lysosomal inhibition. Bafilomycin A1 treatment increased the relative abundance and synthesis of autophagy-associated proteins while decreasing the relative abundance of lysosomal hydrolases. Together, these findings identify neuronal culture medium as a critical determinant of neuronal proteome composition and dynamics and establish a SILAC-compatible BrainPhys formulation for future studies of neuronal proteostasis.
